script.text: A comfortable family car moves through Colombo traffic. Anudi sits in the back seat, looking at her smartphone.
The driver stops near an office building. Anudi gets out, carrying her handbag and umbrella. She thanks the driver and walks toward the building.
Rain begins to fall. She opens her umbrella and continues walking along the roadside, passing Kasun's small food three-wheeler.

advice: Use the final passage to establish proximity, not an exchange with anyone at the business.
Keep the phone in her right hand, handbag on her left shoulder and umbrella in her left hand throughout.
Preserve the onset of rain after the dry approach; the lighting remains overcast throughout.
The acknowledgment is a small nod, without invented dialogue.
treatment.logline: Anudi leaves the shelter of a family car and enters the everyday roadside world where an ordinary encounter will soon become possible.
treatment.approach: Play the hopeful romantic drama through ordinary proximity, not portent: phone attention gives way to a modest acknowledgment and purposeful walking. Seven economical four-second sources separate the vehicle stop, exit, door closure, walking, umbrella opening and onward passage so each change is clear and editable. The 28-second bin exceeds the 23-second target only to provide these necessary action boundaries; trim handles toward the intended duration. No romantic reaction or new encounter is invented.
treatment.geography: The family car travels and stops facing screen right near an office building. Its pavement-side rear door faces camera. Anudi exits onto the pavement, closes that door, and moves screen right toward the building, passing the parked food three-wheeler along that route. Keep all roadside cameras on the pavement side of this travel axis; do not show anyone at the business.

editor_notes: Seven must sources total 28 seconds. They are consecutive pieces of the intended action, not alternate coverage; trim their handles to approach the 23-second scene target.
c01 establishes the moving cabin and Anudi's phone attention; c02 establishes the stopping point; c03, c04 and c05 separate exit, door closure and the walk to the building.
c03 opens with the rear door already open. Cut past its opening; c04 explicitly closes it before c05 begins. The tighter, forward pavement-side setup for c04 avoids a same-size jump after c03.

c06 opens with Anudi paused and the umbrella folded; c07 opens with it already open. Match the left-hand umbrella, right-hand phone, left-shoulder handbag, screen-right travel and light rain across the cut.

The handbag and folded umbrella are already with Anudi in the back seat; the packet does not specify their initial placement. The driver remains seated in the car and no occupant is shown at the food three-wheeler.
Play the acknowledgment as a small silent nod; no dialogue is supplied. Build traffic, door, footsteps, umbrella and rain from separate sound in post, with rain beginning at c06.
All camera sources are clean. Any speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in or split screen is a post choice, not an in-camera effect; none is required for this grounded scene.
Avoid mirrors, body contact, fast hand detail and sharply resolved crowds. The umbrella opening and door closure are isolated practical actions; no encounter or pocketing is invented.

left.sentence: The bin holds 28 s of takes and may hold 23 s (the scene's 23 s x 1): 28 s must, 0 s should, 0 s nice. Drop nice clips first, then should; the must clips are never the ones to go.
